source: Casework and furniture as model elements (Q6422). Casework is read from the plan and its schedule (casework.read); furniture from furniture plans and the furniture drawn in rooms (a block named for it, an outline on a furniture layer, an outline labelled with its name) and repeated into the rooms of the same type the plans leave empty. A size the documents give wins; the heights below are generic trade sizes, used only where no document gives one, and every element that takes one is marked generic with this source.

casework.source: kitchen and bath cabinet industry sizes (base cabinet 34-1/2 in with a 1-1/2 in top: counter at 36 in; wall cabinet bottom 54 in, 30 in tall; vanity rim at 34 in, the most ADA 2010 606.3 allows for an accessible lavatory; tall cabinet and wardrobe 84 in). An AFF height on the plan or in the schedule is the top of a floor-standing item and the bottom of a wall-hung one (the usual reading; the other reading is noted on the element).

furniture.source: common furniture sizes (the standard mattresses 38 x 75, 54 x 75, 60 x 80 and 76 x 80 in, a bed's top about 24 in; desk and table tops 29 to 30 in; seats 17 to 19 in, chair backs about 32 in, sofa backs about 34 in; dressers about 36 in, nightstands about 26 in, armoires about 72 in)

repeat.basis: repeated from a room of the same type that draws its furniture (the plans furnish one typical room): its outline matches this room's
